paragraphs: Powys covers a large rural area in the middle of Wales, and its council fostering service, Foster Wales Powys, is run from County Hall in Llandrindod Wells with offices in Newtown and Brecon. It is one of the 22 not-for-profit council fostering services in the Foster Wales network. Children from Welshpool, Newtown, Brecon, Llandrindod Wells and the villages in between are looked after by its carers and by the services shown above.

The council says anyone with a spare bedroom can apply. There is no upper age limit, you can be single, married or in a civil partnership, and renting or working full time does not rule you out. Care ranges from a few hours a week or a weekend to a year or longer, and new carers can be paired with a mentor in their first months after approval.

Foster Wales Powys publishes its pay in detail. It describes a child's allowance of £250 a week, depending on age, and a carer's fee of between £250 and £1,164 a week, depending on experience and the type of fostering, with extra payments for birthdays, religious festivals, mileage and equipment. It also offers retainer payments between placements, a family leisure pass, free parking in council car parks, Cadw membership, paid membership of The Fostering Network, and five days' extra leave for council staff who foster. A full-time team member gives carers financial advice, and two more support carers' own children.

The Welsh minimum allowance for 2026-27 runs from £208 to £260 a week depending on the child's age, so ask every service what it pays above that. Our Wales page explains the national picture, and our Wrexham, Monmouthshire and Carmarthenshire pages cover nearby areas. Talk to Foster Wales Powys and one or two of the services above before you decide.
